title: The Poor Man's Rembrandt Project
description: Tattoo artist Henk Schiffmacher and his team set up studio inside Rembrandt's house, inking original Rembrandt-inspired designs on visitors: the tattoo as the affordable old master.

title: The Land of Chocolate Sprinkles. Building a new world together
description: Congolese collective CATPC shows 30 sculptures cast in cacao, palm oil and sugar, plus embroideries on cacao sacks, funding the buy-back of exhausted plantation land.

title: Keerthana Kunnath - Not What You Saw
description: The London-based photographer's first museum exhibition, portraying female bodybuilders in Kerala with equal strength and softness to unsettle regional ideas of gender and beauty.

title: Middle East Archive - Al Nisa / Women
description: Two-part Foam project in Amsterdam-West: Yomna El Beyaly solo at Mercatorplein (to 29 Oct) and the group show Al Nisa / Women at MAQAM (to 20 Dec), curated by Romaisa Baddar.

title: the ESSENCE
description: A show tracing graffiti's cultural roots through names, tags, lines and repetition: the building blocks of a visual language born from movement and marking presence.

title: Experimental Urge
description: Over 80 works on paper, from Rembrandt to living artists, tracing how printmakers and draughtsmen kept pushing techniques and materials. Visitors can draw their own work in the gallery.

title: Marcos Kueh: PRESENT
description: Four woven tapestries by Malaysian textile artist Marcos Kueh in the Red Bedroom, a last love letter to his father that echoes the canopy of the empty four-poster bed.

title: Unfinished Pasts: Return, Keep, or...?
description: Steps into the live restitution debate, exploring dilemmas and stories behind contested colonial-era objects.

title: Yoshitoshi. Master of the Moon
description: Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's print series 'One Hundred Aspects of the Moon' shown at the Van Gogh Museum for the first time: warriors, lovers and mythical beings in bold colour.

title: Tales of Two by YONK
description: An interactive digital-puppetry installation by The Hague studio YONK, where visitors use gestures to guide animated characters into shared stories.

title: Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor
description: The first retrospective in the Netherlands devoted to James McNeill Whistler (1834–1903): painter, printmaker, aesthete and enfant terrible.

title: Rembrandt Open Studio
description: Fifth edition: artists Marije Gertenbach and Shani Leseman take over working studios inside Rembrandt's house, with visitors able to watch them at work from 13 November to 10 January.

title: Pioneers of Media Art: The First Years of MonteVideo
description: A group show with LI-MA tracing the first years of MonteVideo, the Netherlands' pioneering video-art gallery, from 1970s electronic imagery to today's immersive artists.

title: The Best Dutch Book Designs 2025
description: The annual selection of the best-designed Dutch books of 2025, chosen by a professional and a student jury, in the centenary year of the first selection.

title: Document Netherlands: New Energy
description: Photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen documents the Dutch energy transition: towering wind turbines, thick undersea cables and colossal platforms on the open sea.

title: Yayoi Kusama
description: Landmark retrospective spanning more than seven decades of Kusama's work: painting, sculpture, installation, drawing, fashion, collage and happenings.

title: Adam Pendleton — Some Wild Kind of Language
description: Pendleton's first museum exhibition in the Netherlands: eleven paintings and eight large-scale drawings exploring abstract form, most of them never shown before.

title: Willem de Kooning at Work
description: A century after de Kooning left the Netherlands for New York, a retrospective of more than 120 drawings with celebrated paintings and sculptures, made with the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Hailun Ma - Hometown
description: The Chinese photographer's first major solo show outside China: recent series on family, youth and daily style in Xinjiang, where fashion becomes a lens for social observation.

title: Myriam Boulos - A Collective Diary: Sexual Fantasies
description: First museum solo show of Lebanese photographer Myriam Boulos, 19th Foam Paul Huf Award winner: a collective diary centred on her series Sexual Fantasies, mostly made in Beirut.

title: Cabinet of Stories: Change the World, Not Us
description: A World Pride show drawing on the archaeology, book and theatre collections to surface forgotten LGBTIQ+ stories across history.

title: Nadav Kander - The Edge of Things
description: Four decades of Nadav Kander's photography, from his Prix Pictet-winning Yangtze River series to portraits of Obama and David Lynch, drawn together by fragility, time and quiet intensity.

title: Ulrich Seidl – Über das Leben, die Liebe und den Tod
description: The first comprehensive Dutch exhibition on Austrian filmmaker Ulrich Seidl, gathering early, little-known and newly commissioned film works about ordinary lives in late-capitalist society.

title: Adolphe de Meyer: The Substance of a Venetian Dream
description: The first European museum show of a rediscovered set of 75 photographs by fashion pioneer Adolphe de Meyer, documenting his life in Venice's Palazzo Balbi-Valier between 1904 and 1909.

title: Andrzej Steinbach: Hier
description: A first Dutch introduction to Andrzej Steinbach's meticulously composed photography, treating seeing itself as an aesthetic problem across typologically organised series.

title: Maya Inès Touam: Belongings
description: The French-Algerian artist's first solo Dutch museum show, presenting digital collages built from hundreds of photographs that explore migration, motherhood and displacement.

title: Hella de Jonge – Dichter bij hun ziel
description: 37 paintings and two sculptures by Hella de Jonge exploring war, family trauma and collective memory rooted in her Jewish family's history.

title: Chez Matisse - Masterpieces from Centre Pompidou
description: Over eighty works from the Centre Pompidou trace Matisse's hunt for balance between colour, form and simplicity, alongside Picasso, Rothko and Barnett Newman.

title: Play!
description: Hands-on pop-up on how games travel the world, from the 4,500-year-old Royal Game of Ur and Mahjong to Tetris and Mario, all playable.

title: Junk Space: Claiming Public Spaces
description: Artists reclaim the anonymous city of malls, infrastructure and forgotten corners, after Rem Koolhaas's "Junkspace", in a show made with Museum MORE.

title: Amsterdam – A Work of Art
description: Iconic 17th-century cityscapes showing how Amsterdam depicted itself as a wealthy, innovative world power as it transformed into a global trading hub.

title: Art Is Not a Crime
description: Photographer Henry Chalfant's documentation of graffiti culture, curated by SUSO33 with archival material from the Dutch Graffiti Library linking his lens to the Dutch graffiti scene.

title: WORN: Treasured Clothing
description: Twenty-four worn, altered and reused garments dating from 1640 to 1930, from embroidered 17th-century mules to a dress passed down through generations of the Six family.

title: Vincent Ruijters - Crimson Gilt
description: An installation of more than a thousand knitted strips in gold and crimson conjures the ghost of the East Indiaman Amsterdam: gold for trade and prosperity, red for colonialism and exploitation.

title: Abracadabra: Mysteries from Houdini to Hans Klok
venue: Joods Museum (Jewish Museum, Jewish Cultural Quarter)
description: The golden age of magic through its Jewish illusionists, from Harry Houdini to Hans Klok, with tricks visitors can try themselves.

title: Do It Yourself! On Cassette
description: Free mini-show in the museum's Studio on Dutch DIY cassette culture, from VPRO's Radiola Improvisatie Salon to the Carcassettes label, with clips to listen to.

title: Stephan Vanfleteren - Transcripts of a Sea
description: Five years of photographing the coastline from northern France to the southern Netherlands: Vanfleteren's sea shifts room by room from glassy calm through misty drift to storm.

title: Atlantic Window IV: Sedrig Verwoert
description: Choreographer Sedrig Verwoert traces dance in the diaspora, pairing a travelogue of his research into Winti, Kawina and Tambu in Suriname and Curacao with the dance film Strange Fruit 2.0.

title: Plantation along the Canal: Stories of People and Power
description: Explores how two of the house's 18th-century residents built their wealth on plantation trade, with an audio tour guided by a descendant of an enslaved woman from Suriname's Jagtlust plantation.

title: Plantation along the Canal
description: Stories of people and power: how Amsterdam's grand canal houses were financed through colonial trade and plantation slavery, told through residents and descendants of the enslaved.

title: The Art of Transformation
description: A theatre-history show on crossdressing, the Slingelandt theatre and revue star Louisette, exploring how costume and staging reshape identity.

title: Recent Additions to the Collection in the Art Gallery
venue: Joods Museum (Jewish Museum, Jewish Cultural Quarter)
description: Five years of acquisitions in the Art Gallery, from contemporary art to objects of Jewish firms and societies and personal mementoes of Holocaust victims.

title: Post/No/Bills #7 — Kexin Hao: Anatomy of Obstruction
description: Kexin Hao turns the corridor around the historic staircase into a body, with large anatomical drawings that read institutions as organisms, from lungs to kidney stones.

title: Disco
description: A tribute to disco's roots in Black, Latino and queer underground clubs, with tracks, videos, art, fashion and design celebrating freedom.

title: Mire Lee: Vomit My Blessing
description: South Korean artist Mire Lee installs a moving, almost-living structure of silicone, steel, motors and liquids exploring desire, decay and transformation.

title: Common Practice — Collaborations in Art and Design
description: The Stedelijk's biennial group show, this edition on collectives such as Hackers & Designers and Image Acts, from artworks and social design to manifestos and printed matter.

title: White Plays Black: Blackface on the Dutch Stage
description: How Dutch theatre normalised blackface, from medieval 'Moors' and 1840s minstrel shows to Zwarte Piet, told through the theatre collection with work by Kara Walker and Brian Elstak.

title: Rembrandts Craftsmanship
description: Five hands-on 'masterclasses' in Rembrandt's technique and tactics, with his etchings, paintings and a drawing, ending in a slow-looking room with The Anatomy Lesson of Jan Deijman.

title: Eva Gonzalès. A New Perspective
description: The first ever retrospective of French artist Eva Gonzalès (1847–1883), gathering her delicate paintings and pastels from international museums and private collections.

title: Drawing!
description: Over 100 drawings from European and American collections chart the revolution in drawing around 1600 led by Hendrick Goltzius, Jacques de Gheyn II and Abraham Bloemaert.

title: August Sander
description: A spring 2027 exhibition of the German photographer August Sander, known for his portraits of Weimar-era society; the museum will publish full details later.

title: Stathis Logothetis: Earth to Earth
venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
description: Retrospective of painter Stathis Logothetis (1925-1997): about 70 works and unpublished archive material, his first retrospective since 1994.
venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

title: Jani Christou: Enantiodromia
venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
description: First major museum show on composer Jani Christou (1926-1970), drawn from his archive, shown to the public for the first time.
venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

title: William Kentridge: Imitate the Sleep of Stones
description: The museum's first solo Kentridge show sets his Orpheus and Eurydice works among kouroi, sphinxes and funerary antiquities.

title: Pylos of Nestor: A Mycenaean Kingdom Revealed
description: 214 objects from Messenia trace a Mycenaean power centre and the Palace of Nestor at Ano Englianos, with excavation diaries and archival photographs.

title: An Ode to Things. Niki Kanagini. Retrospective
venue: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
description: Retrospective of Greek artist Niki Kanagini (1933-2008), from tapestries to participatory installations, with works from a promised family gift.
venue_address: Kallirrois Ave. & Amvr. Frantzi Str. (Former FIX Factory), 117 43 Athens, Greece

title: The Cult of Beauty
venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
description: How ideals of beauty were built, from Antiquity to the cosmetics industry, and a case for the bodies they leave out. Adapted from a Wellcome Collection show.

title: Sim Acquisition, Drawing and War
description: Nearly 100 newly acquired drawings by José Luis Rey Vila (Sim), a key visual chronicler of the Spanish Civil War: quick pencil and charcoal sketches of soldiers, bombings and civilians.
venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

title: 50 anys dels concerts de la Transició. Barcelona, Palau d'Esports
description: Fifty years on from the 1975-76 Palau d'Esports recitals by Raimon, Lluís Llach and Pi de la Serra, told through photographs, period material and concert footage.

title: Visibles
description: Women in rural and farming Catalonia, through Llerona farmer Rosa Pruna i Esteve and four decades of rights won since the EU's 1986 directive on self-employed women.

title: Archive Drops: "We are the Shipyards"
description: A small display of documents about the Royal Shipyards from the museum's archive, with Braille and audio-described material.
venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

title: Premis Enjoia't 2026
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: 30 pieces from the 29th Enjoia't Contemporary Jewellery Awards organised by A-FAD: 15 professional and 15 student works by makers from more than ten countries.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: Extramural project. Dora García
description: The museum's third Extramural edition: artist Dora García stages performances and interventions around Barcelona, treating the city as a space for critical thought.

title: (Un)ravelling trajectories
description: University of Barcelona Fine Arts alumni from the 'Cicle de Retorn' project in dialogue with alumni in the Suñol Soler Collection, including Ignasi Aballí and Susana Solano.
venue_address: Carrer de Mejía Lequerica 14, 08028 Barcelona, Spain

title: World Press Photo 2026
venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
description: The world's best-known photojournalism show returns: all 2026 World Press Photo winning images and multimedia projects from 42 photographers across six world regions.

title: Mater is the ultimate punk: The Analogue Rhizome
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: A MATERFAD pop-up of eight fashion collections by Bau master's students, mixing biomaterials, 3D printing, light and craft to rethink fashion and nature.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: Wounded Militiaman: The Recovery of an Irredeemable Painting
description: Francisco Mateos's Civil War propaganda painting, irreversibly deteriorated, is shown alongside AI-generated imagery that recovers its original visual impact.
venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

title: Una fuerza del pasado
description: Works mainly from the "la Caixa" contemporary art collection that confront art history and tradition, titled after a Pasolini poem.
venue_address: Av. de Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia, 6-8, 08038 Barcelona, Spain

title: Gaudí-Miró-Gomis: Deconstructed
description: Miró sculptures and prints and Joaquim Gomis's Gaudí photographs meet Tomorrow Bureau's AI, 3D-scan and animation installations. With the Fundació Joan Miró.

title: Invisible Animals
venue: Museu Blau – Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona
description: Myth, life, extinction, de-extinction: animals we rarely see, from legendary beasts and extinct species to little-known living ones vital to healthy ecosystems.
venue_address: Plaça Leonardo da Vinci, 4-5, Parc del Fòrum, 08019 Barcelona

title: Barcelona School of Architecture in shaping everyday life in the city (1875–2025)
description: Works and writings by ETSAB faculty trace how architecture, planning and landscape shaped daily life in Barcelona, with a focus on the sea.
venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

title: KBr Flama'26
description: Sixth edition of KBr's showcase of emerging photographers from Barcelona's schools: Sara Bravo, Elena Bulet i Llopis, Meghan Mathews and Luca Gaetano Pira.
venue_address: Torre Mapfre, Avinguda del Litoral 30, 08005 Barcelona

title: Anna Moreno. The Third Twist
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: Recent works by Anna Moreno on utopian architecture, centred on The Terminal Beach, a road-movie film about Ricardo Bofill's unfinished 1979 settlement in the Algerian Sahara.

title: Dana Lixenberg. American Images
description: Retrospective of Dana Lixenberg's three decades of large-format portraits in the US, from Tupac and Biggie to Imperial Courts in Los Angeles and Shishmaref, Alaska.
venue_address: Torre Mapfre, Avinguda del Litoral 30, 08005 Barcelona

title: Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme. Prisoners of Love: Until the Sun of Freedom
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: First exhibition in Spain by Palestinian duo Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme, centred on their audiovisual installation Prisoners of Love and its layered stories of resistance.

title: Spiral of Time – Plaça dels Àngels – MACBA
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: Edwin van der Heide's site-specific sound work, recording the ambient sounds of Plaça dels Àngels since July 2024 and playing them back as a shifting sonic portrait of the square.

title: Divided
description: London artist and publisher Camilla Wills (Divided Publishing) takes over the foyer, part of the Espai 13 season from 6:12 pm to 5:48 pm.

title: The Secret Life of Plants. Anselm Kiefer in the Grothe Collection
description: Barcelona's first major Anselm Kiefer show: around forty paintings, sculptures, installations, photographs and artist's books, mostly from Hans Grothe's collection, on memory, matter and knowledge.

title: Instrumental Baschet. La utopia ressonant
venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
description: The sound sculptures of Bernard and François Baschet, 1950s inventors who built electricity-free instruments from steel, aluminium, cardboard and inflatable cushions.
venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

title: Opening the Archive 08. Le gros orteil.
description: Miró's newly donated drawing Untitled (1930) shown with his sketches for the series, likely inspired by Georges Bataille's essay 'Le Gros Orteil'.

title: Pau Casals a Puerto Rico
venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
description: For Casals' 150th anniversary, the first show of the archive from his last 18 years in Puerto Rico (1955–73), founding institutions, conducting and composing.
venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

title: Music for a problem
venue: Museu de la Música de Barcelona
description: Installation by Gerard Valverde Ros and Marc Villanueva: a magnetic instrument for remixing recordings of Barcelona's 1989 Contemporary Music Week.
venue_address: L'Auditori, Carrer de Lepant 150 (2nd floor), 08013 Barcelona

title: Charlotte Perriand. Free to Rethink the World
description: Spain's first exhibition on Charlotte Perriand, the pioneering modernist designer from Le Corbusier's atelier and a lifelong friend of Sert and Miró.

title: André Ricard. Disseny en ús
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: A survey of André Ricard, a pioneer of contemporary Catalan design, focused on everyday objects conceived as tools serving people and society.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: Asunción Bastida
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: Rediscovers Asunción Bastida (1902-1995), the Barcelona couturier who was the only woman in the top circle of Spanish haute couture, showing collections from Madrid to New York.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: A Journey Through Time at the Royal Shipyards of Barcelona
description: The story of the Drassanes Reials from their 13th-century origins under Peter III to today: the world's largest surviving medieval shipyards.
venue_address: Avinguda de les Drassanes, s/n, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

title: Aurèlia Muñoz. Beings
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: A full survey of textile artist Aurèlia Muñoz, from early collages and embroideries to unseen large macramé structures, her iconic kite-sculptures and late handmade-paper installations.

title: Pere Portabella: The Committed Gaze
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: Screenings of Pere Portabella's films from the MACBA Collection for his centenary: radical cinema made under censorship that rejects linear narrative and treats form as a political stance.

title: Echoes: Videos from the Han Nefkens Foundation Donation
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: Collection display of videos by artists from around the world, donated by the Han Nefkens Foundation, where documentary and poetic moving images are shaped by texture, sound and materiality.

title: Counter-Information: Video-Nou / Servei de Vídeo Comunitari
venue: MACBA – Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona
description: Collection display tracing Video-Nou and the Servei de Vídeo Comunitari, a collective that used video as a tool of political counter-information in Catalonia from 1977 to 1983.

title: Tiburones. Los guardianes del océano
description: Australian Museum show on 450 million years of sharks: ten life-size models from great white to Helicoprion, a megalodon jaw to touch, interactives and an oceanarium.

title: Aurèlia Muñoz. El tèxtil com a pretext
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: For the Aurèlia Muñoz Year, three early textile works from the collection: the 1961 tapestry La Barcelona gòtica and two 1962 screen-printed jute table covers.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: The Reverse Journey. A Sound Fresco through Romanesque Art
description: Ona Balló's sound installation in the Romanesque galleries, playing recordings from six Pyrenean churches whose apse murals now hang in the museum.
venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

title: LED LIGHT
description: Barcelona artist Victor Ruiz Colomer closes the Espai 13 season with work driven by thermodynamics and how Sert's building shapes movement through it.

title: Soy Asurbanipal, rey del mundo, rey de Asiria
description: Assyrian treasures from the British Museum trace the life of Ashurbanipal (669-631 BC): warrior, scholar, lion hunter and builder of a great library.
venue_address: Av. de Francesc Ferrer i Guàrdia, 6-8, 08038 Barcelona, Spain

title: La Cuina de Frankfurt (1926 – 2026). Disseny i gènere a l'espai domèstic
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: For its centenary, Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky's 1926 Frankfurt Kitchen and how industrial design reshaped housework, women's roles and the modern home.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: Picasso and architecture
description: How Picasso's cubist space shaped modern architecture, from Guernica's 1937 pavilion and his Barcelona architects' college friezes to his influence on Le Corbusier.

title: Vectors. Art digital per pensar el futur
venue: Disseny Hub Barcelona – Museu del Disseny
description: A survey of contemporary digital art by artists working with computational technologies, from generative art and live creation to critiques of the invisible infrastructure of the digital world.
venue_address: Plaça de les Glòries Catalanes, 37-38, 08018 Barcelona

title: The Atomic Age
venue: CCCB – Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
description: 20th- and 21st-century art responding to the atom and the bomb, from early physics and mysticism to nuclear protest. Adapted from the Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris show.

title: «Així és la guerra...». Diaris personals de combatents (1936-1939)
description: The Spanish Civil War through combatants' personal diaries: fears, routines, drawings, poems and songs, with the notebooks treated as an exceptional historical source.

title: Jujol, by Perejaume
description: The MNAC's first major Josep Maria Jujol show, curated by artist Perejaume from the architect's newly donated archive, with works by Gaudí, Taut, Tatlin and Matisse.
venue_address: Palau Nacional, Parc de Montjuïc, Barcelona

title: Penny Siopis. Ink, blood and history
description: South African artist Penny Siopis links personal and collective memory, apartheid and colonial repression across painting, drawing and film.

title: Tàpies, Portabella: Politics of Friendship
description: For Pere Portabella's centenary: his lifelong friendship with Tàpies, from the early Franco years on, as a model of alliances between art and politics.

title: Cristina Lucas. E-conmotion
description: Cristina Lucas traces four industrial revolutions, from coal to AI, as battlegrounds of power and colonialism, with triptychs made from each era's materials.

title: Being Related: Shared Language, Shared Knowledge?
description: Video installation on endangered languages and family, with community members documenting their languages, made with the Endangered Languages Archive.

title: A Country in a Container – The Disposal of East German State Symbols
description: What became of the GDR's flags, emblems and medals after 1990: dumped in containers, sold at flea markets, and still shaping how Germany remembers.

title: Helmut Newton's One-off Album
description: A unique album Newton assembled in 1999 for collector Gert Elfering, shown in Berlin for the first time: hand-annotated small prints, Polaroids and outtakes.

title: Scandal! Hermione von Preuschen and the “Mors Imperator”
description: The painter, writer and traveller whose 1887 painting Mors Imperator, rejected by the Berlin Academy of Arts, made her famous overnight.

title: Rooms / Stages
description: Helmut Newton Foundation group show on space as stage: a dozen artists' rooms, sets and deserted interiors beside Newton's hotel-suite fashion shoots and murals.

title: Between the Lines: Daniel Libeskind and the Jewish Museum Berlin
description: For the building's 25th anniversary, drawings and models trace how Libeskind's 1989 competition design became one of the most influential museum buildings. Free.

title: 3hd 2026: Beyond Imagining
description: A video programme by Creamcake exploring how the real and the invented bleed into each other, with work from four artists on power, identity and institutional critique.

title: Manatunga: Artistic Interventions by George Nuku
description: Three large interventions by Māori artist George Nuku in two rooms of the Oceania galleries, made in polystyrene and Plexiglas during his Collaborative Museum fellowships.

title: Gabriele Stötzer: Dabei sein und nicht schweigen
description: The largest institutional solo show yet of East German artist Gabriele Stötzer: about 150 works in painting, photography, textile, Super 8 film and performance on justice, gender and resistance.

title: Friends for the Arts of East Asia in Berlin
description: Marks 100 years of the Society for East Asian Art with museum holdings and loans, including an 18th-century Japanese Buddhist painting.

title: 100 Years of the Dictionary of the Egyptian Language
description: In the Mythological Hall, a centenary show on the Egyptian Dictionary, begun in this building in 1897 from over a million hand-copied index cards.
venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

title: Digital Sovereignty Experience Space
description: Free, hands-on space by the MobilitätDigital initiative in Hall 6 of the Ladestraße: VR accident replays, AI avatars and an image-recognition challenge on data and AI in mobility.

title: The Portrait of the German Chancellor: First Unveiling of the Official Portrait of Former Chancellor Angela Merkel
description: Jérémie Queyras's official portrait of Angela Merkel, Chancellor for 16 years, on public display for the first time before it joins the Chancellery's gallery.
venue_address: Am Kupfergraben (entrance via Monbijoubrücke), 10178 Berlin, Germany

title: Courage: Sisters in Spirit
description: The Prater Galerie's reopening show: eight women artists, pairing GDR-era collection works by Jetelová, Vent and Schulze Eldowy with contemporaries from Eastern Europe.

title: Ruin and Rush. Berlin 1910–1930
description: Around 35 collection works by Dix, Höch and others on Berlin between war, excess, poverty and emancipation in the 1910s and 1920s.

title: Shilpa Gupta: What Still Holds
description: Works by Shilpa Gupta on language, borders and power, in direct dialogue with Joseph Beuys and the Marx Collection.

title: Rafik Greiss: The City and the City
description: Rafik Greiss's first institutional solo show premieres a new film essay drifting through Cairo, Alexandria and the Western Desert on time, memory and history.

title: CHANEL Commission: Lina Lapelytė. We Make Years Out of Hours
description: Lina Lapelytė turns the Historic Hall into a polyphonic stage for a participatory choreography.

title: Susan Hiller: Bad Dreams
description: The first Berlin survey of Susan Hiller, a pioneer of conceptual and video art, with hypnotic audiovisual installations probing fantasy, fear and the unconscious.

title: Daniel Chodowiecki, 1726–1801. Images of the Enlightenment in Berlin
description: A cabinet show marking the 300th birthday of Chodowiecki, star of late-18th-century Berlin, with 20+ of his key works on the Enlightenment's social questions.

title: KOO JEONG A: OUSSSEAN
description: KOO JEONG A's first major solo show in Germany: multisensory environments of light, scent, sound and temperature, reconfigured for KW's architecture.

title: Destiny in the Stars: The Beginnings of the Zodiac
description: The history of the zodiac from Babylonia to Egypt and the Greco-Roman world, from star tablets to celestial ceilings.
venue_address: Bodestraße, 10178 Berlin (visitor entrance via the James-Simon-Galerie)

title: Founded on Antiquity: Berlin's First Museum
description: The upper-floor show revisits the museum's 1830 beginnings, reuniting antiquities from its first display around a large model of Schinkel's original building.

title: The Opposite of Now
description: Twelve contemporary art projects, by Yael Bartana, William Forsythe, Alexander Kluge and others, imagine paths to a different present. Old Building, level 1.

title: Lauren Greenfield: Social Studies
description: Lauren Greenfield's social experiment on growing up in the digital age: teenagers, selfies and the pressures of social media.

title: Miji Ih: Mouths: On Water and Whisky
description: Miji Ih's largest solo show: photography, archive material, sound and video on "comfort women" and the lives of women around US military bases in Japan, South Korea and Germany.

title: InterNationalgalerie 1: National Museum in Warsaw

title: Georg Baselitz: Meine Schule
description: Georg Baselitz's last completed paintings and sculptures, curated by Richard Calvocoressi, at 555 West 24th Street; the gallery's first Baselitz show since his death in April.

title: 25th Anniversary Exhibition: Masterworks from the Neue Galerie
description: Opening Autumn 2026, this milestone show fills the entire museum with collection highlights, from Klimt's Adele Bloch-Bauer I to German and Austrian masterworks and Wiener Werkstaette design.

title: Ragtime: Cakewalk in Pianoland
description: Early printed ragtime and cakewalk music from the John Davis Collection of Early Printed Musical African Americana, setting Ernest Hogan beside Scott Joplin.

title: Rothko/Gottlieb: The Surrealist Years
description: Paintings and works on paper by Mark Rothko and Adolph Gottlieb from 1941 to 1951, when both turned to myth and Surrealist abstraction. Curated by Arne Glimcher.

title: Na Mira: NO SMOKING
description: Na Mira's first solo museum exhibition in New York: a newly commissioned media installation in the Kravis Studio using radio frequencies, infrared heat and holography, drawing on Korean shamanism and structural filmmaking.

title: The Nature of Color
description: An interactive exhibition on what color reveals about the natural world and ourselves, from how animals and plants use it to how it shapes mood.
venue_address: 200 Central Park West, New York, NY 10024, United States

title: Alex Webb: Walking Blues
description: Magnum photographer Alex Webb's bold-colour street pictures from some forty US cities, shaped by the rhythm of blues music over more than a decade.
venue_address: 380 Columbus Avenue at West 78th Street, New York, NY 10024

title: artport: A History of Internet Art
description: Marking the 25th anniversary of the Whitney's artport platform, this show gathers over 100 commissioned net-art works charting the evolution of internet art from 2001 to 2024.

title: Imitation of Life
description: World premiere musical with a book by Lynn Nottage and music and lyrics by John Legend, directed by Liesl Tommy. Two mothers, one Black and one White, raise their daughters across 1920s Atlantic City and 1930s New York.

title: Éliane Radigue: States of Listening
description: Co-organized with Blank Forms, this show restages French composer Éliane Radigue's pulsating 1970s sonic installations in Dia's program space, with live synthesizer and acoustic performances.

title: Virgil Abloh: The Codes
description: A survey of Virgil Abloh's work in fashion, art, architecture and music: nearly 1,000 objects from his archive over 28,000 sq ft, including a recreation of his Paris office.

title: Across Wine-Dark Seas: Art and Identity beyond Ancient Greece
description: Presents more than 180 exceptional works exploring art and identity beyond ancient Greece.

title: Farah Al Qasimi: TAILSPIN
description: A video exhibition exploring American industry, oil culture and Arab immigration through the perspective of a jinn, blending documentary footage and personal testimony to examine identity in post-9/11 America.

title: Sixth New Museum Triennial: The Outside Expands
description: The sixth edition of the museum's signature international triennial for early-career artists, co-curated by Vivian Crockett and Isabella Rjeille, examines how artists destabilize fixed notions of territory, identity, gender, and sexuality.
venue_address: 235 Bowery, New York, NY 10002, United States

title: Sonya Kelliher-Combs: TITIQ/MARK
description: Nearly two decades of work by Iñupiaq and Koyukon artist Sonya Kelliher-Combs (paintings, sculptures and installations on history, cultural continuity and land use), her first solo museum show in New York.

title: Woody De Othello: coming forth by day
description: Miami-born Woody De Othello's new ceramic and wood sculptures, tiled wall works and a large bronze, his first institutional solo show in New York, travelling from Pérez Art Museum Miami.

title: William Blake: Paradise Lost
description: For the 200th anniversary of Blake's death, his Milton-inspired watercolors, illuminated books and paintings reunited, with works by Fuseli and Flaxman.

title: Plumes from Paradise
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: From the forests of New Guinea to the paintings of Northern School masters, a journey tracing five centuries of fascination with birds of paradise.

title: Nanténé Traoré — pays des merveilles
description: A MEP Studio show pairing an analogue photographic project shot in Brittany in 2025 with expired 1990s film stock, and a film made during a 2026 Albania residency, exploring memory, dissociation and disorientation tied to the artist's childhood on the Breton coast.

title: Mungo Thomson: Monument
description: The Californian artist presents "Snowman," a bronze sculpture inspired by cardboard tubes, and "Time Life Volume 15," a stop-motion film built from thousands of book images, subverting the idea of a monument through everyday materials and collective memory.

title: La saison américaine du musée de l'Armée
description: A season marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, with displays on key figures and Franco-American military ties, plus concerts, talks and film screenings.
venue_address: Hôtel national des Invalides, 129 rue de Grenelle, 75007 Paris, France

title: Affinities: Islamic Art Wonders in the Department of Decorative Arts
description: Around 50 Islamic artworks from the 9th to 17th centuries set among European decorative arts, revealing how Eastern techniques of light, colour and sculpture inspired Western craft.

title: Marie and Félix Bracquemond, Decorative Arts Drawings
description: A display in Room 33 of the 2024 gift of nearly 200 drawings by the Impressionist Marie Bracquemond and engraver Félix Bracquemond, focused on their decorative-arts designs.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Talisman
description: To mark the bicentennial of Gustave Moreau's birth, the museum gives contemporary painter Ali Banisadr carte blanche, staging an intergenerational dialogue between his work and Moreau's Symbolist legacy.
venue_address: 14 rue de la Rochefoucauld, 75009 Paris, France

title: Hosts at the Louvre: Kader Attia and Elizabeth Peyton
description: Contemporary artists Kader Attia and Elizabeth Peyton present the results of their two-year Louvre residencies, offering intersecting interpretations of the museum and its collections.

title: La Bataille des couleurs
description: Inaugural show at Maison Pompidou (50 rue Rambuteau) on the Centre's now-iconic colour-coded palette, and the gold, blue and brown that nearly won, told through architecture documents, photos and design objects.

title: Statue de la Liberté : reportage photographique à la fin du XIXe siècle
description: A dozen-plus reproductions of 19th-century archive photos from the museum's collection, following the Statue of Liberty from the Gaget workshops to its Atlantic crossing.

title: Yu Nishimura: Towards a Sea
description: The Japanese painter's first major institutional solo show in France, around fifty drawings and large-scale paintings of landscapes inhabited by human and animal figures, with the sea as a recurring motif.

title: Hélène Fauquet: Vivresse
description: The artist's first French institutional show, pairing sculptures shaped by shells with works exploring decoration versus conceptual art, using photography, ornamental forms and advertising-derived bubble motifs to probe nature and artifice.

title: Parcours : Pablo Picasso au prisme de « Cahiers d'Art »
description: A focus room marking the centenary of the review Cahiers d'Art: 30+ works it reproduced, setting Picasso beside Rousseau, Miró, Dalí and Max Ernst.

title: Echoes of the Invisible
description: An Orsay Lab display in Room 8 pairing collection works with a video made with adolescents in psychiatric care at Pitié-Salpêtrière, on mental health and emotion.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Florian Krewer: woven thin
description: The German painter's first solo show in France: sixteen monumental, expressionistic canvases installed within the museum's permanent collection display, including previously unseen works.
venue_address: 11 Avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: The Chamber of Echoes: The Blue of Everything
description: Charles Villa's sun-bleached flower postcards, which UV light turned blue, beside Yto Barrada's 16mm film The Power of Two or Three Suns, in the free entrance area.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Zeus, le cheval métallique au MuAM
description: A monumental metallic horse sculpture from the 2024 Paris Olympics opening ceremony, installed on the museum's forecourt with free public access.

title: The World According to Penn
description: Nearly 450 photographs by Irving Penn, from the 1940s to the early 2000s, shown in a non-chronological installation spanning portraits, fashion, ethnographic reportage, nudes and still lifes in Gallery 2.

title: Stan Douglas: Parallax
description: The most significant Paris survey of Canadian artist Stan Douglas in over 30 years, spanning film, video, photography and installation that probe how history is constructed, represented and transmitted.
venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

title: Céleste Richard-Zimmermann: Not All Columns Have a Heart of Stone
description: The Prix des Amis du Palais de Tokyo winner turns the space into an abandoned quarry of sculptures, bas-reliefs and sound works around a huge, broken column.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Andy Warhol. La ligne et l'image
description: About 150 drawings, plus paintings, silkscreens, photographs and archives, trace Warhol's drawn work from a 1942 self-portrait to The Last Supper in 1986.

title: Maurice Denis, Illustrating Christian Mysticism
description: Around 246 recently acquired sheets trace Maurice Denis's decades-long project to illustrate "The Imitation of Christ," shown alongside his paintings and other works on Christian and spiritual subjects.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Michel Lacoste's Donation: Precious Metalwork from Pierre Mangot to Jean-Elisee Puiforcat
description: Around one hundred pieces of precious French metalwork from the 16th to 20th centuries, donated by Michel Lacoste, showcasing the technical skill and refinement of French silversmiths.

title: Cézanne and Us
description: Nearly 180 works tracing Cézanne's profound influence, from Gauguin, Matisse and Picasso to Mondrian, Joan Mitchell and Peter Doig, and the artists who claimed his legacy.
venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

title: Cezanne et nous (Cezanne and Us)
description: Some 180 works (70 by Cezanne) trace his profound influence on modern art from the 1880s to today, the 'father of us all' as Picasso put it. At the Grand Palais, co-produced with the Pompidou and Musee d'Orsay.

title: PENN & FASHION
description: A chronological retrospective of Irving Penn's fashion photography from 1947 to 2008, spanning his Parisian haute couture images of the 1950s through collaborations with Issey Miyake, John Galliano and Chanel, drawn from the MEP and Nicola Erni collections.

title: EVERYDAY CLOTHES
description: A family-oriented show for young visitors, staged in dialogue with PENN & FASHION, exploring what everyday clothing (creases, stains, mends, signs of wear) reveals about the people who wore it, drawn from the MEP's collections.

title: Vertigo: Richard Peduzzi at Orsay
description: Marking the museum's 40th anniversary, this show revisits set designer Richard Peduzzi's original 1986 scenography for Orsay through his theatre and opera models, drawings and sculptures.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: First Nations
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: Arts and culture of the Northwestern United States, exploring First Nations artistic traditions featuring mythical beings and spirit animals such as the Raven.

title: Open Space #19: Mohammad Alfaraj
description: Saudi artist Mohammad Alfaraj's first solo show in a French institution, "I'd rather be a dragonfly than a lion" brings stop-motion videos, objects, photographs and drawings drawn from the oral traditions and landscape of the Al Ahsa oasis to Gallery 8.
venue_address: 8 Avenue du Mahatma Gandhi, 75116 Paris, France

title: Remember Me
description: Marking photography's bicentenary, this major group show gathers around 700 works by more than 70 artists from Gustave Le Gray to today, anchored by a Barbara Kruger commission in the Rotunda.

title: Simone Fattal: Des villes au fond d'un lac
description: Major retrospective of Lebanese-American artist Simone Fattal, around one hundred works over fifty years, from early landscape paintings to ceramics and collages.
venue_address: 11 Avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: "I Spend My Life Painting"
description: To mark the centennial of Claude Monet's death, a dedicated itinerary through the Impressionist Gallery (Rooms 29 to 35) celebrates his life and work.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Kerry James Marshall: The Histories
description: First exhibition in France devoted to American painter Kerry James Marshall, around seventy works including eight new paintings, exploring Black representation and art history.
venue_address: 11 Avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Timeless Tintoretto
description: The first comprehensive survey in France of the Venetian master Tintoretto, tracing his audacious compositions and dramatic light from the Renaissance to his influence on 19th-century French painting.

title: Nicolas Flamel, alchimiste de papier
venue: Musée de Cluny - musée national du Moyen Âge
description: The real Nicolas Flamel: not the immortal alchemist of legend but a 15th-century Parisian scribe, donor and property investor, traced through his tombstone and archives held at Cluny.

title: Monet, Painting Time
description: Marking the centenary of Monet's death, this exhibition traces how his painting engaged with time, from the Cathedrals, Haystacks and Poplars series of the 1890s through to the Water Lilies, drawing largely on the Musée d'Orsay and Musée Marmottan Monet collections.
venue_address: Jardin des Tuileries, Côté Seine, 75001 Paris, France

title: Zurbarán: 1598–1664
description: A major retrospective of the Spanish Golden Age painter Francisco de Zurbarán, spanning his monumental monastery commissions, portraits and still lifes alongside his influence on later French avant-garde artists.

title: Sculpting Colour: Masterpieces from the Museo Nacional de Escultura, Valladolid
description: 17th-century Spanish polychrome wooden religious sculptures, including a complete processional float by Gregorio Fernández with five life-size figures displayed at eye level.

title: Dimanche sans fin: Maurizio Cattelan and the Centre Pompidou collection
description: For Centre Pompidou-Metz's 15th birthday, hundreds of collection works (Breton's studio wall, Duchamp's chess table) and pieces by Cattelan riff on the idea of 'Sunday' across 27 thematic rooms.

title: Raymond Depardon
description: Around fifty photographs from the Pinault Collection by photojournalist Raymond Depardon, drawn from his long-term documentary series "La France" on provincial landscapes and small towns, shown in Gallery 3.

title: The History of Tears
description: American artist Barbara Kruger fills the Rotunda and Display Cases with filmed sequences, audio clips, and text-and-image lightbox installations exploring emotion, power, and desire.

title: To Open Eyes: Regards d'artistes
description: At Centre Pompidou Malaga, a thematic journey through 20th- and 21st-century art from the Musee National d'Art Moderne collection, in six interconnected sections about how artists make us see differently.

title: Mary Cassatt. Being Independent
description: Co-organised with London's National Gallery and Boston's MFA for Orsay's 40th anniversary, this retrospective of nearly 80 paintings, pastels and prints traces Mary Cassatt's career through her guiding principle of independence.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Vies minuscules
description: Around thirty artists from Kupka to Jumana Manna, drawn from the Centre Pompidou's collections, fill the Pantheon's nave with quiet, intimate and anonymous lives - a counterpoint to the monument's great men. Free entry, part of the Constellation programme.

title: See Tahiti. Early Photographs, 1859-1870
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: A rare photographic collection from French Polynesia's earliest decade of photography, featuring works by naval officers Gustave Viaud and Paul Emile Miot.

title: A Statue for Liberty, Bartholdi's Dream, from Paris to New York
description: An exclusive virtual reality experience running alongside the Bartholdi exhibition, covering almost 700 m² in the Museum's Amont Gallery to trace the Statue of Liberty's journey from Paris to New York.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Auguste Bartholdi. Liberty Enlightening the World
description: Marking 250 years of American independence, this exhibition and an accompanying VR experience trace how sculptor Auguste Bartholdi conceived and built the Statue of Liberty.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Parcours : André Malraux et Pablo Picasso, le musée imaginaire
description: A focus room on André Malraux's view of Picasso, born of his 1973 visit to the artist's last home and studio and his book La Tête d'obsidienne.

title: Prix Marcel Duchamp 2026
description: The four 2026 nominees for France's leading contemporary art prize (Andrianomearisoa, Brognon Rollin, Henno, Ntjam) show work within the MAM's collections. Winner announced 22 October 2026.
venue_address: 11 Avenue du Président Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Kurt Schwitters. Le chaos-monde, 1918-1948
description: First Kurt Schwitters retrospective in France in over thirty years: 300+ works and documents, from Merz collages to the Ursonate, set beside his affinities with Picasso's assemblage.

title: Wild Heart
description: Sonia Gomes's textile-based sculptures draw on Afro-Brazilian heritage, transforming fabric and craft into vehicles of memory, care and resistance.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Ali Cherri: Today Is Ok
description: French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri presents the film "La Sentinelle" and a new installation on military service and its psychological effects, following a soldier suspended between destiny and self-abandon.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Rose Lowder: The Source of the Loire and Other Films
description: Filmmaker Rose Lowder's fifty-year research into visual perception through nature observation, centred on her film "La Source de la Loire" (2019-2021) alongside twenty one-minute films shot on organic farms in southern France.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Fragments of Paris: Jacques Villeglé and Urban Art
description: A retrospective marking the centenary of Jacques Villeglé, tracing his practice of collecting torn Parisian street posters and reworking them into art that documents the city's changing urban and cultural landscape.

title: Photoromance
description: The first major French solo show of Ivorian photographer Paul Kodjo, co-produced with Les Rencontres d'Arles: his 1970s photo-novels and documentary images of Abidjan.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Valerie John: I Telman Nwe Ki I Ble (So Black It Turns Blue)
description: Valerie John explores indigo blue as material, memory and artistic gesture, with assemblages of paper, textiles and objects tracing cultural ties between Martinique and West Africa.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Lassana Sarre: Globale Inversion Inversion
description: Painter Lassana Sarre creates wall paintings and looped sound installations celebrating the overlooked routines and shared meals of the Palais de Tokyo's security staff.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: You and Your Gang
description: A group exhibition of individual and collective artistic practices rooted in non-urban territories across France, including Limousin, the Cevennes and Corsica.
venue_address: 13 Avenue du President Wilson, 75116 Paris, France

title: Contemporary Counterpoint: Vija Celmins
description: The museum's 17th Contemporary Counterpoint: Vija Celmins's precise studies of ocean, desert, sky and snow surfaces, made 1971-2000 in drawing, painting, printmaking and wood engraving, shown in the pronaos and contemporary gallery in dialogue with Monet's Water Lilies.
venue_address: Jardin des Tuileries, Côté Seine, 75001 Paris, France

title: Louise Bourgeois: Extreme tension
description: The BnF and Centre Pompidou combine their Louise Bourgeois holdings for the first time - some 200 drawings, prints and artist's books - in the artist's first Paris public-institution show since 2008. At the BnF Richelieu, Galerie Mansart.

title: Jenny Holzer. J'ai vu
description: A museum-wide activation by American artist Jenny Holzer: LED installations, facade projections and carved stone benches drawing text from Orsay's 1848-1914 collection.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Echoes of the Tides
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: An installation by Yo-E Ryou in the music box of the Collections Plateau, unfolding through sound, breath and duration to explore resonance between bodies, water and memory.

title: The Harvest Season - Ibrahim Mahama
description: Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama's first major French show, with nine associate artists, reactivating African independence-era utopias through monumental installations made from salvaged materials.

title: Moteur Imaginaire
description: Large's opening show, curated by Cecilia Alemani: works from Renault's art collection beside 17 new commissions, over 100 works by 55 artists on humans, factories and machines.
venue_address: 3 parvis Amont, Île Seguin, 92100 Boulogne-Billancourt, France

title: Susan Meiselas: Nicaragua, History, Memory
description: Meiselas's 1978-79 Sandinista revolution photographs and how they took on a life of their own on objects and murals: 100+ works, documents and film clips, curated by Clément Chéroux.

title: Martine Franck: Images, Press and Feminist Struggles
description: Mostly unpublished photographs by Martine Franck of 1970s feminist movements, mainly in Paris: protests and the feminist press. Curated by Angèle Ferrere.

title: Gustave Fayet, Collector - Designer. Icons of Modern Art
description: Rediscovery of Gustave Fayet (1865-1925), pioneering collector of van Gogh, Gauguin and Picasso and a prolific designer, drawing on loans from 64 institutions and 71 private collections.
venue_address: 8 Avenue du Mahatma Gandhi, 75116 Paris, France

title: Primeval Waters: Lessons from Mesopotamia
description: An exploration of ancient Mesopotamia's relationship with water, tracing early canals and aqueducts and the environmental consequences of humanity's first great hydraulic engineering.

title: Paolo Cirio: NUDIFY AI
description: An online commission in which Paolo Cirio investigates non-consensual AI-generated sexual imagery, turning 15,000 collected deepfakes into an anonymised visual database.
venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

title: Louvre Photo
description: Over 300 photographs tracing the Louvre's own history, from the invention of photography to today, showing the museum as subject, model and source of inspiration.

title: Lady Liberté. De la sueur, de l'audace, du génie
description: An immersive look at how the Statue of Liberty was built in 1880s Paris, tracing the copper, iron and ingenuity, including Gustave Eiffel's internal frame, behind the Franco-American monument.

title: Transparency
description: Inaugural show of the new Palais des enfants: a playful, sensory journey where artworks and science experiments play with light to spark the curiosity and wonder of very young visitors.
venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

title: Guillermo Kuitca, Chapelle
description: A site-specific installation by Argentine artist Guillermo Kuitca in the chapel of the Hôtel Salé, where his "cubistoid" intersecting lines are painted directly onto the walls to form a new pictorial space.

title: New Paris, from 1977 to the Present Times
description: A free display in the 1977-to-today room on how Paris has changed since its first elected mayor, with recent acquisitions by Christo and Jeanne-Claude, JR and others.

title: Silent Violence: Through the Eyes of Romeo Mivekannin
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: Artist Romeo Mivekannin uses mirror effects and metal sculptures to examine the history of colonial exhibitions and human zoos, reinterpreting historical ethnographic photographs from the museum's collection.

title: Gustave Le Gray, Painter and Photographer
description: A "Bicentennial of Photography" retrospective on Gustave Le Gray (1820-1884), the painter-turned-photographer and technical innovator, featuring newly surfaced acquisitions shown for the first time.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Travail, ce que disent les objets
description: A capsule show in which some thirty Cnam and CNRS researchers pick everyday work objects, from office chair to badge and post-it, illustrated by Romain Joly, to show how work is changing.

title: Révéler. Collection de photographie du Centre Pompidou
description: About a hundred works by some thirty artists from the Centre Pompidou's photography collection, shown at the Grand Palais during Paris Photo 2026 for the bicentenary of photography.

title: De Gaulle avant de Gaulle
description: Charles de Gaulle's early military and literary career, 1909 to 1940, before his famous June 1940 appeal, told through letters, manuscripts, photographs and personal objects.
venue_address: Hôtel national des Invalides, 129 rue de Grenelle, 75007 Paris, France

title: Le Musée imaginaire d'Oli
description: The rapper Oli (Bigflo & Oli) stages his inner museum: about a hundred works and new installations, laid out as a coming-of-age journey with sound as the thread.
venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

title: David Gilbert — Apparitions
description: The first French solo exhibition of American artist David Gilbert, gathering fifteen years of work at the intersection of photography, sculpture and installation: studio-built assemblages of paper, fabric and found objects photographed as fragile, twilight-lit tableaux.

title: Girls. Adolescence, Fashion and Rebellion
description: Artists, designers, photographers and filmmakers challenge traditional representations of teenage girls through multidisciplinary works spanning fashion, photography, film and contemporary art.
venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

title: Édouard Vuillard
description: A Room 33 display of recent Vuillard gifts, including two overdoor panels completing the Public Gardens series and pieces from the Schopfer dinner service.
venue_address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

title: Mika Ninagawa with EiM: Alive with Shadows
description: An unprecedented European exhibition of Japanese visual artist Mika Ninagawa's work alongside her creative collective EiM, exploring beauty, transience and the interplay of light and shadow through photography, video and installations.
venue_address: Avenue du Général Eisenhower, 75008 Paris, France

title: Le sentiment du monde. Carte blanche au Centre Pompidou
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: The Centre Pompidou hangs works by several generations of artists inside the museum's permanent route, setting formal echoes and critical reinterpretations of tradition against the collections.

title: Aïnous. Une voix du Japon
venue: Musée du quai Branly - Jacques Chirac
description: The first exhibition by a French national museum on the Ainu, Indigenous people of northern Japan. Contemporary Indigenous art links past and present, with loans from Japan's national Ainu museum.

title: William Klein: New York Revisited
description: Klein's 1954-55 New York photographs, drawn from his studio's documents: icons of 20th-century photography and many images the tight layout of the 1956 book hid, with the first full reading of this body of work.
venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

title: Jonathas de Andrade: Tropical Hangover and Other Stories
description: The Brazilian artist's relationship to the image, through key projects of the past decade in photography, video and installation.
venue_address: 1 place de la Concorde, Jardin des Tuileries, 75001 Paris, France

title: Frankenstein Pop-Up
description: The museum's popular Frankenstein pop-up returns for spooky season, on view on select Saturdays from September through November.
venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

title: An Endless Meeting: Featuring Caroline Woolard
description: Caroline Woolard's installation brings together works from "A Stone Holds Water" (2020) and "Art of Gravity" (2026).
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: An Endless Meeting: Collective Process, Artistic Labor, and the Politics of Working Together
description: New Red Order, Kameelah Janan Rasheed and Caroline Woolard each approach collaboration, shared knowledge and collective action through distinct forms.
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: An Endless Meeting
description: Vox's autumn project on collective process, artistic labour and the politics of working together, spanning exhibitions, a curatorial residency, public programmes and a print publication.
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: An Endless Meeting: Featuring New Red Order
description: New Red Order's "Give it Back: Crimes Against Realty (Office Edition)" is a real estate office and recruitment station encouraging the rematriation of land to Indigenous people.
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: An Endless Meeting: 變 SLOW BURN
description: Eight artists and collectives work through memory, grief, queer kinship and transformation in installation, performance, video, sound and painting, drawing on fènghuáng mythology.
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: An Endless Meeting: Still Taking Minutes
description: Curated by Logan Cryer, an interview-based show about how Philadelphia artists build, sustain and leave collectives, with new work by Aaron Terry, Ollie Goss, Gregory Donnell Parker and catia colagioia.
venue_address: 319 North 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107, United States

title: Revolutionary Botany
description: Marking America's 250th birthday, this show traces the origins of American pharmacy and botanical medicine in the city that called itself the birthplace of American medicine.
venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

title: The Philly Killer
description: Summer 1976: as Philadelphia threw America's Bicentennial party, a deadly unidentified pneumonia struck. The true story of Legionnaires' disease.
venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

title: Kati Gegenheimer: We've Only Just Begun
venue: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
description: A Morris Gallery monographic show in which Gegenheimer's vivid paintings and mixed-media works treat love, familial and romantic, as an aesthetic and political structure rather than a sentiment.
venue_address: 118-128 North Broad Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102, United States

title: Marketing Medicine: The Art of Selling a Cure
description: Two centuries of medical trade ephemera show how jingles, patient testimonials and celebrity endorsements taught medicine to sell itself.
venue_address: 19 S. 22nd Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, United States

title: Creating a City of Medicine
description: 250 years of Philadelphia's impact on how Americans have learned, taught, practised and experienced medicine, told through the College's own archive.
