venue_address: 401 Richmond St. W, Suite 120, Toronto, ON M5V 3A8, Canada

title: Magnus Hara: The Light of Day
description: Vases by 2024 Gardiner Museum Prize winner Magnus Hara, altering and combining familiar forms as a reclamation of joy and autonomy after grief, loss and injury.
venue_address: 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C7, Canada

title: Richard Avedon Immortal: Portraits of Aging, 1951–2004
description: Nearly 100 Avedon portraits confronting aging, from Toni Morrison to the Dalai Lama, plus a restaging of his 1974 MoMA series on his father Jacob Israel Avedon.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: Tanya Marcuse: Portent
description: A multichannel video of ominous natural scenes, from swaying trees to volcanic vapour, on the New Media Wall, drawn from Marcuse's Book of Miracles series.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: Molly Steels: I Am/Was/Always
description: Family archives, pressed flowers and a lakeside video explore grief, mortality and the women who came before. Student Gallery.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: Psychedelics: Art. Culture. Science.
description: A research-driven look at the cultural, historical and scientific significance of psychedelics through artworks, objects, botanical specimens and interactives.
venue_address: 100 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C6, Canada

title: Things Fall Apart
venue: Art Museum at the University of Toronto
description: The fourth Toronto Biennial of Art, curated by Allison Glenn, explores rupture through the Great Lakes and global waterways, across both campus galleries.
venue_address: University of Toronto Art Centre, 15 King's College Circle, Toronto, ON M5S 3H7; Justina M. Barnicke Gallery, 7 Hart House Circle, Toronto, ON M5S 3H3

title: In Search of Imperfection: The Macdonald Collection of Japanese and Japanese-Inspired Ceramics
description: The Macdonald Collection shown in full for the first time: early Edo-period Japanese porcelain and Japanese-inspired ceramics, explored through nature, leisure and global trade.
venue_address: 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C7, Canada

title: Always In Fashion
description: Curated by Amber-Dawn Bear Robe, an immersive look at how contemporary Indigenous couturiers blend ancestral knowledge with innovation, featuring Kent Monkman, Brian Jungen and more.
venue_address: 55 Centre Avenue, Toronto, Ontario M5G 2H5, Canada

title: Critical Minerals: Critical Choices
description: Gallery installation in Earth's Treasures on the minerals essential to a net-zero society, and the lifestyle choices tied to them.
venue_address: 100 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C6, Canada

title: Crawford Lake: Layers in Time
description: How sediments of a small lake near Milton, Ontario record 1,000 years of human impact, making it the "golden spike" candidate for the Anthropocene.
venue_address: 100 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C6, Canada

title: Rouzbeh Akhbari: Of Wool and Diesel
venue: Mercer Union, a Centre for Contemporary Art
description: A film installation tracing sheep smuggling and seafaring histories along a trade corridor from Azerbaijan to Oman, with archival material and handmade felt works.
venue_address: 1286 Bloor Street West, Toronto, ON M6H 1N9, Canada

title: Michael Massie: now and then
description: Career survey of Inuk silversmith and sculptor Michael Massie: iconic teapots, unexhibited pieces and new large-scale installations full of joy and humour.
venue_address: 199 Richmond St. W., Toronto, ON M5V 0H4, Canada

title: Returning to Ourselves: Rebecca Baird and Kenny Alvin Baird—A Retrospective of Art and Design by Cree Métis Siblings
description: Forty years of sculpture, painting, traditional materials, interior and graphic design, film art direction and public art by Cree Métis siblings Rebecca and Kenny Baird.
venue_address: 199 Richmond St. W., Toronto, ON M5V 0H4, Canada

title: Chinese Zodiac Case: Year of the Horse
description: ROM's annual zodiac installation marks the Year of the Horse with horse figures from early China, once placed in tombs to serve the dead.
venue_address: 100 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C6, Canada

title: Made By Many: 50 Years of the Textile Museum of Canada
description: A 50th-anniversary show tracing five decades of exhibitions back to the 1970s, with works by Bev Koski, Marimekko, Melinda Patterson, Thor Hansen, You Wenfeng and more.
venue_address: 55 Centre Avenue, Toronto, Ontario M5G 2H5, Canada

title: Beverly Glenn-Copeland: Light of the Heavens
description: The South Stairwell Sound Series plays a recently recovered c.1986 song by Canadian composer Beverly Glenn-Copeland, from the Keyboard Fantasies era.
venue_address: 158 Sterling Rd, Toronto, ON M6R 2B7, Canada

title: Delcy Morelos: Ombligo
description: A site-specific installation by Colombian artist Delcy Morelos: sisal rope, soil and Toronto-harvested corn roots swell from the ceiling of Floor 2.
venue_address: 158 Sterling Rd, Toronto, ON M6R 2B7, Canada

title: Bharti Kher: Bones
description: Fifteen years of Bharti Kher's assemblages: sari-clad hybrid figures, stone and concrete forms and bindi-covered paintings, with a monumental new tondo.
venue_address: 158 Sterling Rd, Toronto, ON M6R 2B7, Canada

title: Northumberland
description: Boxing photographer Pete Doherty weaves ring images with photos of his dying parents and their Ontario town into a portrait of a life remade by loss.
venue_address: 401 Richmond St. W, Suite 120, Toronto, ON M5V 3A8, Canada

title: Spotlight: Spanish Holbein Carpet
description: A 15th-century carpet from Alcaraz, Spain, on loan from MFA Boston, where Muslim weavers blended Turkish designs with Iberian techniques.
venue_address: 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1, Canada

title: Torkwase Dyson: The Distance Inside Us (Bird and Lava)
venue: The Joan and Martin Goldfarb Gallery of York University (formerly AGYU)
description: Across all three galleries, Torkwase Dyson's painting, sculpture, drawing and animation use abstract "Hypershapes" to explore liberation, confinement and ecological crisis.
venue_address: 83A York Blvd, Toronto, ON M3J 1P3, Canada

title: Jeanne Randolph with John Monteith, Fabulous Neoconstantinopolitanism
venue: The Joan and Martin Goldfarb Gallery of York University (formerly AGYU)
description: Randolph's recluse La Betty staged with Vasarely, Albers and Motherwell from York's collection and a rug by John Monteith. Visible Vault; fully open Wed and Sat.
venue_address: 83A York Blvd, Toronto, ON M3J 1P3, Canada

title: Saks Afridi: SpaceMosque
description: Saks Afridi's speculative sci-fi narrative uses recovered artifacts, sound and archives to trace a mysterious vessel said to answer collective prayers.
venue_address: 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1, Canada

title: Zadie Xa with Benito Mayor Vallejo: Moonlit Confessions Across Deep Sea Echoes: Your Ancestors Are Whales, and Earth Remembers Everything
venue: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
description: Paintings, murals, sound and a conch-shaped mobile of 600+ brass bells weave Korean mythology, diaspora and marine ecology into a multi-sensory installation.
venue_address: 231 Queens Quay West, Toronto, Ontario M5J 2G8, Canada

title: Sharon Lockhart: Fogo
venue: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
description: Sharon Lockhart's Fogo Island Portrait Studio photographs and the film installation WINDWARD, a long, attentive look at Newfoundland's Fogo Island and its people.
venue_address: 231 Queens Quay West, Toronto, Ontario M5J 2G8, Canada

title: Owner of a Lonely Heart
venue: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
description: An 80-minute looping film program by Haig Aivazian, Stephanie Comilang, Alia Farid, Hope Pearl Strickland and Yuyan Wang on labour, ecosystems and commodities.
venue_address: 231 Queens Quay West, Toronto, Ontario M5J 2G8, Canada

title: André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled
description: Over 95 designs by André Perugia (1893-1977), pioneer of the stiletto heel, made for Dior, Schiaparelli, Josephine Baker and other clients.
venue_address: 327 Bloor Street West, Toronto, ON M5S 1W7, Canada

title: Toronto Biennial of Art at the Aga Khan Museum
description: Contemporary works from the Toronto Biennial of Art 2026 across the park, atrium, façade and galleries, including Dawit L. Petros. Free to visit.
venue_address: 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1, Canada

title: After the Island: Caribbean Canadian Ceramics
description: PJ Anderson, Eddy Firmin, Manuel Mathieu and Sharon Norwood use clay to explore Caribbean diaspora memory, identity and belonging, in partnership with BAND and MoAD.
venue_address: 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C7, Canada

title: Retracing Tatreez: Palestinian Thobes through the 20th Century
description: Palestinian embroidered thobes and jellayeh from the collection, most shown for the first time, curated by Nina Rafique with restored context on their regional motifs and journeys.
venue_address: 55 Centre Avenue, Toronto, Ontario M5G 2H5, Canada

title: Over and Over Again
venue: Art Museum at the University of Toronto
description: Carol-Ann Apilado, Kuh Del Rosario, Sukaina Kubba and Esmelyn Miranda Orozco use weaving to probe broken patterns. At the Jackman Humanities Institute, Mon–Fri 9–4.
venue_address: University of Toronto Art Centre, 15 King's College Circle, Toronto, ON M5S 3H7; Justina M. Barnicke Gallery, 7 Hart House Circle, Toronto, ON M5S 3H3

title: Dawoud Bey: Material Histories, Living Landscapes
description: Dawoud Bey's landscape photographs and the two-channel video 350,000 meditate on North American land and Black diasporic history, with works from the AGO's Frum Collection.
venue_address: 317 Dundas Street West, Toronto, Ontario M5T 1G4, Canada

title: Kamrooz Aram: Lapis Intervention
description: Artist Kamrooz Aram co-curates a gallery intervention setting his lapis-blue Arabesque paintings among collection works to challenge Eurocentric display.
venue_address: 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1, Canada

title: Adaptive Ceramic Histories
description: Medical and adaptive ceramics made for sick or disabled users, from the 17th century to today, seen from the patient's side of care. Curated by Alexandra Box.
venue_address: 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C7, Canada

title: Cao Fei: Isle of Instability
description: Cao Fei's 2020 multimedia installation, commissioned by Audemars Piguet Contemporary, on the Salah J. Bachir New Media Wall. Guest curator Simone Estrin.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: Donna Gottschalk: We Others
description: Photographs by American photographer Donna Gottschalk in the Main Gallery, guest-curated by Hélène Giannecchini.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: Lee Shulman & Omar Victor Diop: Being There
description: Photographic collaboration between Lee Shulman (The Anonymous Project) and Omar Victor Diop. University Gallery, curated by Gaëlle Morel.
venue_address: 33 Gould Street, Toronto, ON M5B 1W1, Canada

title: The Tarbouche. When an Accessory Becomes a Symbol
venue: Palazzo Mocenigo – Museum of Textiles and Costume
description: Lebanese artist Mouna Rebeiz sets the tarboosh on monumental female nudes, using the traditional headgear to question femininity, beauty and the hidden meaning of accessories.

title: The Silks of Lucio Andrich
venue: Palazzo Mocenigo – Museum of Textiles and Costume
description: Silk panels by Lucio Andrich (1927-2003), pieced from Missoni and Como fabric offcuts and hand-stitched by Burano embroiderer Maria Tagliapietra: Dolomite legends to lagoon fauna.

title: Paulo Nazareth. Algebra
description: Brazilian artist Paulo Nazareth fills the former customs house with twenty years of work tracing colonial fractures, threaded by a line of salt outlining a ghost slave ship.

title: In Minor Keys – 61st International Art Exhibition
description: Koyo Kouoh's Biennale Arte 2026, completed by her team after her 2025 death: 110 artists across the Giardini, Arsenale and Venice, tuned to earth, life and quiet signals.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Japan Pavilion: Grass Babies, Moon Babies – Ei Arakawa-Nash
description: For the pavilion's 70th anniversary, Ei Arakawa-Nash merges art and parenting: visitors carry one of 200 baby dolls through the gardens and Yoshizaka's building.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Leiko Ikemura. TransLucent — La forma della luce
description: Leiko Ikemura's glass sculptures placed among the permanent collection, in dialogue with masters from Paolo Veneziano to Giambattista Tiepolo.
venue_address: Campo della Carità, Dorsoduro 1050, 30123 Venezia, Italy

title: Lorna Simpson. Third Person
description: Lorna Simpson's largest European show in over a decade: about fifty paintings, collages, sculptures, installations and films on memory, representation and identity.

title: US Pavilion: Call Me the Breeze – Alma Allen
description: Alma Allen's biomorphic sculptures in walnut burl, volcanic rock, Yule marble and bronze explore elevation and transformation of matter, in the Giardini's US Pavilion.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Jenny Saville a Ca' Pesaro
venue: Ca' Pesaro – International Gallery of Modern Art
description: First major Venice show of British painter Jenny Saville: 30+ paintings and drawings from the 1990s to today, ending with new works made in homage to the city.

title: Spiral Economy. Charrière and Canova
description: Julian Charrière's works in dialogue with Canova's marbles in the Canova Galleries, on stone, geological memory and deep time.
venue_address: Piazza San Marco 52, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy (entrance: Ala Napoleonica, monumental staircase)

title: German Pavilion: Ruin – Henrike Naumann & Sung Tieu
description: Henrike Naumann and Sung Tieu use vanished East German sites as blueprints; Tieu wraps the facade in a trompe-l'oeil mosaic of a ruined Berlin housing block.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Nigel Cooke: Bad Habits
description: British painter Nigel Cooke's first solo show in Italy, staged during the 2026 Biennale in the library's portego, transformed into an artist's studio.
venue_address: Santa Maria Formosa, Castello 5252, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

title: Italian Pavilion: Con te con tutto – Chiara Camoni
description: Chiara Camoni fills the Tese delle Vergini at the Arsenale with 24 life-sized sculptures woven from plants, flowers, plastics and debris, curated by Cecilia Canziani.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Bizhan Bassiri. Principe. Il Nottambulo del Pensiero Magmatico
description: Bizhan Bassiri's recent and emblematic works in the Sala delle Quattro Porte, with ninety images of artists from the 15th to 21st centuries in a suspended, stepped display.
venue_address: Piazza San Marco 52, 30124 Venezia VE, Italy (entrance: Ala Napoleonica, monumental staircase)

title: Amoako Boafo
description: Ghanaian painter Amoako Boafo's first solo show in Italy: new finger-painted portraits in dialogue with Venetian portraiture, on the palazzo's second floor.
venue_address: Castello 4858, Ramo Grimani (Ruga Giuffa), 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

title: Corpus serialis
venue: Ca' Pesaro – International Gallery of Modern Art
description: Peruvian artist Nicolás Lamas assembles found objects and fragments into sculptures and installations probing how systems of classification shape what we see.

title: EMPORION – Andrea Valleri
description: Paintings and sculptures by Venetian-born, Greek-adopted artist Andrea Valleri retrace ancient Mediterranean trade routes, fusing classical antiquity with Pop Art.
venue_address: Riva S. Biasio, Castello 2148, 30122 Venezia, Italy (Padiglione delle Navi: Fondamenta dell'Arsenale 2162C)

title: Cosmotechnics: Ding Yi as a Planetary Code
description: Shanghai abstractionist Ding Yi shows new black-and-white paintings and stone steles from his Appearance of Crosses series, curated by Cramerotti and Scalera.
venue_address: Santa Maria Formosa, Castello 5252, 30122 Venezia VE, Italy

title: French Pavilion: Comme Saturne – Yto Barrada
description: Yto Barrada draws on the long history of textile work in a sequence of environments: suspended shapes, a Saturn room of folded wool, and stalling machines.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: British Pavilion: Predicting History: Testing Translation – Lubaina Himid
description: Lubaina Himid's large multi-panel paintings of architects, boatbuilders and tailors debating whether to move or stay probe belonging and making a home somewhere new.
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Alfred Eisenstaedt. La fotografia era nell'aria
description: A century through the lens of the Life photojournalist behind V-J Day in Times Square, from 1930s Europe to portraits of Einstein and Marilyn Monroe. Curated by Monica Poggi.
venue_address: Riva S. Biasio, Castello 2148, 30122 Venezia, Italy (Padiglione delle Navi: Fondamenta dell'Arsenale 2162C)

title: Erwin Wurm. Dreamers
description: First major Italian retrospective of Austrian sculptor Erwin Wurm: One Minute Sculptures, anthropomorphic objects and the body as sculpture, blending humour and philosophy.
venue_address: San Marco 3958, Campo San Beneto, 30124 Venezia, Italy

title: Venice Pavilion: Note Persistenti
description: Curated by Giovanna Zabotti, a lagoon-inspired show with Dardust, Paolo Fantin, Ilya and Emilia Kabakov and Alberto Scodro, opening on a reflecting pool of underwater "notes".
venue_address: Giardini: Viale Trento 1260, 30122 Venezia; Arsenale: Campo della Tana 2169/F, 30122 Venezia, Italy

title: Helter Skelter: Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince
venue: Fondazione Prada Venezia (Ca' Corner della Regina)
description: Nancy Spector curates 50+ works by Arthur Jafa and Richard Prince, two image scavengers who mine American pop culture. Includes explicit content.
venue_address: Calle de Ca' Corner, Santa Croce 2215, 30135 Venice, Italy

title: A Lace for Venice 2026
venue: Palazzo Mocenigo – Museum of Textiles and Costume
description: 43 works from the 12th national lacemaking competition, in needle and bobbin lace on the theme of flowers and nature, from traditional patterns to contemporary takes.

title: Amar Kanwar. Co-travellers
description: Two multimedia installations by Indian artist Amar Kanwar, The Torn First Pages and The Peacock's Graveyard: poetic, political meditations on justice, mortality and impermanence.

title: La Tua Perla per Venezia 2026
description: Finalist works from the international Venetian glass bead competition, shown in the museum's Venetian Bead Room; visitors can vote for their favourite bead.

title: Michael Armitage. The Promise of Change
description: 45 paintings and over 100 studies by the Kenyan-British painter, whose works on Ugandan bark cloth weave East African politics, violence, migration and dreamlike visions.

title: Nel segno di Venezia: The Alessandro Favaretto Rubelli Donation
venue: Ca' Rezzonico – Museo del Settecento Veneziano
description: 29 drawings from a recent donation, from Palma il Giovane's 16th century to Carlevarijs, Ricci, Canaletto and Tiepolo, shown in the first-floor portego.

title: BABEL - Marco Toso Borella
description: About twenty new works by Murano artist Marco Toso Borella, scratched into gold leaf on glass, on incommunicability in an age of social media and AI.

title: Fucina degli Angeli: Peggy Guggenheim and 20th-Century Artistic Glass
description: Postwar Murano glass by Egidio Costantini's Fucina degli Angeli, founded 1955, which turned artists' designs into glass with Peggy Guggenheim's backing.
venue_address: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni, Dorsoduro 701, 30123 Venice, Italy

title: A Muslim, a Christian, and a Jew - Eran Shakine
description: At Dorotheergasse: Israeli artist Eran Shakine's humorous large oil-pastel works follow three top-hatted men, one of each faith, exploring what the monotheistic religions share.

title: JJJJJerome Ellis: An unfinished calendar that commemorates slaves escaping their enslavers, 1673–1886
description: Sheets naming enslaved people who escaped, each with date, place and a painted flower, fill the walls as Ellis's voice reads the names aloud.

title: Lap-See Lam: 192 Wing Lok Street
description: Lap-See Lam's new glass sculptures, sound and spatial objects on diaspora and family history, with bamboo-like glass forms and a soundscape tied to Hong Kong.

title: Bernhard Leitner: SOUNDSPACESCULPTURE
description: Sound pioneer Bernhard Leitner shows new and earlier immersive sound installations, including a water-based sound space and a Sound Couch you feel through your body.

title: ANNEA LOCKWOOD: A SOUND MAP OF THE DANUBE
description: Presented with Wien Modern, Annea Lockwood's multichannel sound installation follows the Danube from the Black Forest to the Black Sea, weaving river sounds with the voices of people who live by it.

title: Herbert Boeckl – Hans Josephsohn: Figural Archetypes
description: Painter Herbert Boeckl and sculptor Hans Josephsohn, who never met, in dialogue: shared ideas of the body, material and the search for form.

title: Otto Meets Albertina
description: German comedy legend Otto Waalkes as painter, sending his Ottifants roaming through art history in dialogue with the Albertina's collection.

title: Bridge of Humanity. Austria and the 1956 Hungarian Uprising
venue: State Hall of the Austrian National Library (Prunksaal)
description: Previously unpublished photographs of Austria's humanitarian response in 1956, when some 200,000 Hungarian refugees crossed the border seeking asylum.

title: The Special Exhibit: Erich Lessing: A Moment of Hope
venue: State Hall of the Austrian National Library (Prunksaal)
description: Erich Lessing's contact sheet from Budapest on 28 October 1956, when the Hungarian Uprising briefly seemed won. Chosen by public vote, shown within Bridge of Humanity.

title: Glaciers out of balance
venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
description: Jürgen Merz's before-and-after photographs retrace 19th-century glacier views across the Alps, showing how fast the ice is retreating. Hallway, level 1.

title: Vasarely & Adrian: Dynamic Grids
description: Op Art pioneers Victor Vasarely and Marc Adrian side by side: geometric grids and optical effects designed to set the viewer's eyes in motion.

title: Erna Rosenstein: On the Other Side of Silence
description: Retrospective of Polish avant-garde artist Erna Rosenstein (1913–2004): some eighty paintings, drawings, assemblages and poems on trauma, memory and resilience.

title: VALLY WIESELTHIER: Ceramic Sculptor
description: A survey of Viennese ceramist Vally Wieselthier (1895-1945), whose expressive ceramic sculpture spanned Europe and America, with many works from her US estate shown for the first time.

title: Innovation Corner: Power Forward
description: Eight energy-storage innovations from VERBUND and Austrian start-ups and researchers, from salt-water and oxygen-ion batteries to green hydrogen and smart EV charging, plus an interactive grid game.

title: Ishír: Living Memories from Paraguay
description: Pop-up show pairing Guido Boggiani's c.1900 photographs and collection with the voices of today's Ishír (Chamacoco) people of Paraguay.

title: Down Syndrom: Über uns, mit uns
description: People with Down syndrome tell their own stories about everyday life, school and work, friendships, hobbies and dreams.

title: THOMAS DEMAND: Rooms That Dream of the Past
description: Thomas Demand turns historic theatre set models, from the Baroque to the early 20th century, into a new photographic series with large wall installations and custom lighting.

title: Picasso - Bacon: What It Feels Like to Be Human
description: Major face-off between the 20th century's two great figurative painters, Picasso and Bacon, and their savage reinventions of the human body.

title: Erika Giovanna Klien: All Is Movement
description: Solo show of Erika Giovanna Klien (1900–1957), leading figure of Viennese Kineticism: birds in flight, dancing bodies, rotating machines and her later New York work.

title: Terminal Piece
venue: mumok – Museum moderner Kunst Stiftung Ludwig Wien
description: A five-act show across five levels built around Kate Millett's 1972 installation, setting some 400 collection works, loans and commissions around the act of looking.

title: More than Recycling
description: A five-level special exhibition on the circular economy: how food, clothing, housing and leisure could be rethought from a product's start, with projects like algae-based clothing.

title: Her Story: Women Artists of the Albertina
description: The first show devoted to the women artists in the Albertina's collection, from medieval convent woodcuts to early feminist work of the 1970s.

title: Seeds: Reclaiming Roots, Sowing Futures
description: Main show of the Klima Biennale Wien: 13 international artists, including Cecilia Vicuña and Kapwani Kiwanga, use sculpture, installation, photography and video to explore seeds, loss and regeneration.

title: Elisabeth von Samsonow
description: First large-scale survey of the Austrian artist-philosopher: sculptures, paintings, drawings, films and a site-specific installation on the earth as bearer of history, life and memory.

title: Shara Hughes: Sink In
description: Fever-dream landscapes by US painter Shara Hughes: giant flowers, enchanted forests and blazing sunsets in fauvist, expressionist colour.

title: Feminist Futures Forever
description: Artists from the feminist avant-garde to today tackle social, gender and ecological issues, building on the landmark 1985 show Kunst mit Eigen-Sinn.

title: ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRUCTION KITS 1890–1990: Plenty to Play With!
description: About 150 building kits from a century of toy-making, from wood and metal to Galalith and Lego, with eight hands-on stations where visitors can play and build.

title: The Special Case of Steffy Goldner: The New York Philharmonic's First Woman
description: In the Dorotheergasse Project Space: Nives Widauer's installation on Vienna-raised harpist Steffy Goldner, projected onto a historic harp case.

title: Farbenspiel. Mode aus vier Jahrhunderten
description: A cultural history of colour told through around 350 garments from the Wien Museum's fashion collection, exploring colour as a symbol of status, emotion and identity.

title: Franz West: The Revolution of Sculpture
description: Retrospective marking Franz West's 80th birthday, centred on his Adaptives: sculptures meant to be worn and handled that blurred art and everyday life.

title: CARLONE CONTEMPORARY: Asta Gröting. Things
description: Asta Gröting's video installation sends deformed everyday objects floating in slow motion through a deep blue summer sky, shown in the Upper Belvedere's Carlone Hall.

title: Crime Scene Ephesus: Cleopatra and Rome
description: A KHM show on the unsolved murder behind an octagonal tomb in Ephesus, set among Cleopatra, Caesar, Mark Antony and Augustus. In the Neue Hofburg.

title: No Way Home: Viennese Jews in Exile
description: At Museum Judenplatz: how Vienna stripped its Jews of their rights after 1938 and drove them out, and the lives of those who fled.

title: Temporary. Structures of Necessity
description: KOSMOS architects look at the temporary structures that keep cities running, from construction sites to maintenance work, and what they reveal about efficiency and adaptability.

title: Documents of Injustice. The Case of Freud
description: The Freud family's last months in Nazi Vienna: the dispossession of Sigmund and Alexander Freud and the murder of their four sisters, told through newly acquired documents.

title: Raining Blood. Photography and Arms Trafficking
description: Photos of c.1900 arms dealers, collection objects and contemporary art trace the global gun trade and challenge colonial myths of 'primitive' weapons.

title: TO SHOE OR NOT TO SHOE. Warhol and others
description: Cabinet show on the women's shoe as fetish, projection surface and site of feminist critique: Andy Warhol's shoe prints alongside Birgit Jürgenssen, Gudrun Kampl and Sylvie Fleury.

title: OPEN SPACE: A Room for Many Voices
description: A participatory room where communities from across Vienna reflect on the world and the museum, with three invited artists. Free admission.

title: Caution, high voltage! Electrical accidents – a class of their own
venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
description: At the NHM's Narrenturm site (Spitalgasse 2, 1090), a show on electropathology: Vienna's pioneering research, electricity's effects on the body, first aid and prevention.

title: Franz West and Vienna
description: How his home city shaped Franz West, focused on his formative years from the late 1960s to the early 1980s. Opens alongside a parallel West show at the Albertina Modern.

title: Hidden Stories: Treasures from the Collections
description: Objects from the Weltmuseum's stores that have rarely, if ever, been on public display, with the stories of where they came from and what they meant.

title: Good Collecting – Bad Collecting. 150 Years of the Natural History Museum Vienna
venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
description: The anniversary show traces how a 30,000-object imperial collection grew into 30 million, and looks critically at the darker sides of collecting and exploration.

title: GENchangers: Unraveled Secrets from Early Medieval Burial Grounds
venue: Natural History Museum Vienna (Naturhistorisches Museum Wien)
description: Genetics and archaeology reveal family ties in two early medieval burial grounds near Vienna, retelling the Migration Period through ordinary people's lives. Hall 21.

title: tierisch menschlich
description: The close yet ambivalent bond between animals and humans, from the Middle Ages to today, with works by Goya, Ensor, Maria Lassnig, VALIE EXPORT and Graciela Iturbide.

title: Tec/xtil
